DUCHESNE COUNTY UTAH COURT

The Duchesne County Utah Court system serves as a vital judicial institution for residents of Duchesne County, providing essential legal services and justice administration. Understanding its structure and services is crucial for anyone needing to interact with the local justice system.

What are Physical Locations and Contact Information for Duchesne County Utah Court

The Justice Court maintains two important addresses for public reference:

  • Physical Address: 799 E 1260 N, Duchesne, UT 84021
  • Mailing Address: PO Box 15, Duchesne, UT 84021

You can reach the Justice Court through multiple channels:

  • Phone: (435) 738-0109
  • Fax: (435) 738-0115
  • Email: jcduchesne@utcourts.gov

Court Jurisdiction and Services

The court system in Duchesne County handles various legal matters, from civil disputes to criminal cases. An important note for visitors: court appearances are by schedule only, with no open court available. All appearances must be arranged through direct contact with the court.

What is Court Structure and Operations of Duchesne County Utah Court

Justice Court Services

The Justice Court handles various cases, including:

  • Traffic violations
  • Small claims disputes
  • Misdemeanor criminal cases
  • Local ordinance violations

The court emphasizes efficiency and accessibility while maintaining strict scheduling protocols to ensure smooth operations.

District Court Operations

The District Court handles more serious cases and larger civil matters, working in conjunction with the Justice Court to provide comprehensive legal services to the community. This coordination ensures that all legal matters are addressed at the appropriate judicial level.

Court Scheduling and Appearances

To maintain efficient operations, the court follows a strict scheduling system. Residents must:

  • Contact the court directly to schedule appearances
  • Arrive at their designated time
  • Follow all court protocols and procedures
  • Prepare necessary documentation in advance

What are Administrative Offices and Services at Duchesne County Utah Court

County Offices Overview

The Duchesne County offices, located at 734 North Center Street, serve as the administrative hub for various county services. The main phone line (435-738-1100) connects residents to different departments.

Department Contact Information

Key county departments and their contact details include:

  • Assessor: 435-738-1110 (PO Box 998)
  • Clerk/Auditor: 435-738-1100 (PO Box 270)
  • HR: 435-738-1233 (PO Box 346)
  • Recorder: 435-738-1160 (PO Box 916)
  • Treasurer: 435-738-1190 (PO Box 989)

Quick Access Services

The county provides various quick-access services for residents, including:

  • Commission minutes access

Conclusion

The Duchesne County Utah Court system, along with its associated administrative offices, provides comprehensive legal and governmental services to county residents. Through its organized structure, scheduled appearances, and various public resources, the court system ensures efficient and accessible justice administration while maintaining strong connections with the community it serves.

FAQs

  1. How do I schedule a court appearance in Duchesne County? Contact the Justice Court directly at (435) 738-0109 or email jcduchesne@utcourts.gov to schedule your appearance, as there is no open court available.
  2. Where can I find property tax information in Duchesne County? Property tax information can be accessed through the county website's quick links section or by contacting the Treasurer's office at 435-738-1190.
  3. How can I access public records in Duchesne County? Public records can be accessed through online portals, in-person requests at the county offices, or by contacting the relevant department directly.
  4. What services does the Duchesne County Justice Court provide? The Justice Court handles traffic violations, small claims disputes, misdemeanor criminal cases, and local ordinance violations.
  5. How can I get involved in Duchesne County government? Residents can participate through boards, commissions, and committees, attend public meetings, or volunteer for community events. Information is available through the county offices or website.
